subject: science
question_text: Why does a compass needle get deflected when brought near a bar magnet?
answer_text: A compass needle is a small bar magnet. When it is brought near a bar magnet, its magnetic field lines interact with that of the bar magnet. Hence, a compass needle shows a deflection when brought near the bar magnet.
final_answer: Therefore, the compass needle deflects due to the interaction of magnetic fields.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of the concept of magnetic interaction.

subject: science
question_text: Draw magnetic field lines around a bar magnet.
answer_text: Magnetic field lines of a bar magnet emerge from the north pole and terminate at the south pole. Inside the magnet, the field lines emerge from the south pole and terminate at the north pole.
final_answer: Thus, the magnetic field lines represent the direction and strength of the magnetic field around a bar magnet.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of magnetic field representation.

subject: science
question_text: List the properties of magnetic lines of force.
answer_text:
The properties of magnetic lines of force are as follows:
(a) Magnetic field lines emerge from the north pole.
(b) They merge at the south pole.
(c) The direction of field lines inside the magnet is from the south pole to the north pole.
(d) Magnetic lines do not intersect with each other.
final_answer: These properties describe the behavior and characteristics of magnetic field lines.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of magnetic field properties.

subject: science
question_text: Why don’t two magnetic lines of force intersect each other?
answer_text: If two field lines of a magnet intersect, then at the point of intersection, the compass needle points in two different directions. This is not possible. Hence, two field lines do not intersect each other.
final_answer: Therefore, magnetic lines of force do not intersect.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of the concept of magnetic field lines.

question_text: Choose the correct option. A rectangular coil of copper wires is rotated in a magnetic field. The direction of the induced current changes once in each

mcq_options.option_text: two revolutions
one revolution
half revolution
one-fourth revolution

answer_text: When a rectangular coil of copper is rotated in a magnetic field, the direction of the induced current in the coil changes once in each half revolution. As a result, the direction of current in the coil remains the same.
final_answer: Thus, the direction of the induced current changes once in each half revolution.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of electromagnetic induction principles.

subject: science
question_text: Name two safety measures commonly used in electric circuits and appliances.
answer_text: Two safety measures commonly used in electric circuits and appliances are as follows: (i) Each circuit must be connected with an electric fuse. This prevents the flow of excessive current through the circuit. When the current passing through the wire exceeds the maximum limit of the fuse element, the fuse melts to stop the flow of current through that circuit, hence protecting the appliances connected to the circuit. (ii) Earthing is a must to prevent electric shocks. Any leakage of current in an electric appliance is transferred to the ground and people using the appliance do not get the shock.
final_answer: Therefore, using fuses and earthing are essential safety measures.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of safety measures in electrical systems.

Hence, the current drawn by the electric oven is 9.09 A, which exceeds the safe limit of the circuit. Fuse element of the electric fuse will melt and break the circuit.

subject: science
question_text: What precaution should be taken to avoid the overloading of domestic electric circuits?
answer_text: The precautions that should be taken to avoid the overloading of domestic circuits are as follows: (a) Too many appliances should not be connected to a single socket. (b) Too many appliances should not be used at the same time. (c) Faulty appliances should not be connected in the circuit. (d) Fuse should be connected in the circuit.
final_answer: Therefore, proper management of appliances and fuses is essential to prevent overloading.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of electrical circuit management.

subject: science
question_text: Which of the following correctly describes the magnetic field near a long straight wire?

mcq_options.option_text: The field consists of straight lines perpendicular to the wire
The field consists of straight lines parallel to the wire
The field consists of radial lines originating from the wire
The field consists of concentric circles centred on the wire

answer_text: The magnetic field lines, produced around a straight current-carrying conductor, are concentric circles. Their centres lie on the wire.
final_answer: Thus, the magnetic field near a long straight wire consists of concentric circles.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires basic understanding of magnetic fields.

subject: science
question_text: The phenomenon of electromagnetic induction is

mcq_options.option_text: the process of charging a body
the process of generating magnetic field due to a current passing through a coil
producing induced current in a coil due to relative motion between a magnet and the coil
the process of rotating a coil of an electric motor

answer_text: When a straight coil and a magnet are moved relative to each other, a current is induced in the coil. This phenomenon is known as electromagnetic induction.
final_answer: Thus, electromagnetic induction is the process of producing induced current due to relative motion.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of electromagnetic induction.

ammeter
motor

answer_text: An electric generator produces electric current. It converts mechanical energy into electricity.
final_answer: Therefore, the device used for producing electric current is called a generator.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of the definition of a generator.

subject: science
question_text: The essential difference between an AC generator and a DC generator is that

mcq_options.option_text: AC generator has an electromagnet while a DC generator has permanent magnet.
DC generator will generate a higher voltage.
AC generator will generate a higher voltage.
AC generator has slip rings while the DC generator has a commutator.

answer_text: An AC generator has two rings called slip rings. A DC generator has two half rings called commutator. This is the main difference between both the types of generators.
final_answer: Therefore, the essential difference is that an AC generator has slip rings while a DC generator has a commutator.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of definitions.

question_text: At the time of short circuit, the current in the circuit

does not change
increases heavily
vary continuously

answer_text: When two naked wires of an electric circuit touch each other, the amount of current that is flowing in the circuit increases abruptly. This causes short-circuit.
final_answer: Thus, the current increases heavily during a short circuit.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of the concept of short circuits.

question_text: A coil of insulated copper wire is connected to a galvanometer. What will happen if a bar magnet is (i) pushed into the coil, (ii) withdrawn from inside the coil, (iii) held stationary inside the coil?

parts.part_text: When a bar magnet is pushed into a coil of insulated copper wire, a current is induced momentarily in the coil.
parts.answer_text: A current is induced momentarily in the coil, causing the galvanometer needle to deflect in a particular direction.
parts.final_answer: Thus, the galvanometer needle deflects momentarily in a particular direction.

parts.part_text: When the bar magnet is withdrawn from inside the coil, a current is again induced momentarily in the coil in the opposite direction.
parts.answer_text: A current is induced momentarily in the opposite direction, causing the galvanometer needle to deflect in the opposite direction.
parts.final_answer: Thus, the galvanometer needle deflects momentarily in the opposite direction.

parts.part_text: When a bar magnet is held stationary inside the coil, no current will be induced in the coil.
parts.answer_text: No current will be induced, hence the galvanometer will show no deflection.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, the galvanometer shows no deflection.

answer_text: A current induces in a solenoid if a bar magnet is moved relative to it. When a bar magnet is pushed into the coil, a current is induced momentarily in the coil. When the bar magnet is withdrawn, a current is induced in the opposite direction. When the bar magnet is held stationary, no current is induced.
final_answer: Thus, the galvanometer shows no deflection when the magnet is stationary.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of electromagnetic induction and its effects.

subject: science
question_text: Two circular coils A and B are placed close to each other. If the current in the coil A is changed, will some current be induced in the coil B? Give reason.
answer_text: Yes, when the current in coil A is changed, the magnetic field associated with it also changes, inducing a current in coil B due to electromagnetic induction.
final_answer: Thus, a current is induced in coil B due to the changing magnetic field from coil A.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the relationship between changing currents and induced currents.

subject: science
question_text: What is the function of an earth wire? Why is it necessary to earth metallic appliances?
answer_text: The metallic body of electric appliances is connected to the earth by means of earth wire so that any leakage of electric current is transferred to the ground. This prevents any electric shock to the user. That is why earthing of the electrical appliances is necessary.
final_answer: Therefore, earthing is necessary to prevent electric shocks.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of electrical safety concepts.
